commits.summary: Add the brief for setup as a tool, revised with the user, and open VF-083 on outside fetching
commits.body:
llm-dlc/loops/in-the-loop-setup-as-a-tool-brief.md is the brief the user will queue next: a /run-setup skill backed by jobs (a verified input lock, a readiness receipt for each pin and task, a setup record in fixed sections), with resolution through a fetch run behind a repository door on loopback. It was written by another agent with the user on top of the first draft (in-the-loop-build-driven-fetch-brief.md), and revised in this session against what the user decided and what was built on 2026-11-28. The first draft stays, with a note at its top that it is superseded and which two things in it no longer hold.

What the revision changed, each at the user's word: the request rule is the one decided and built (one queue for the machine, 0.2 s between two requests to a host, a ceiling that warns), not a second and caps that stop; S48's closure is 282 artifacts, not 770 files; the pin job takes the git mirrors, not the dependency mirror; the level is 'builds'; gate 2 says what it shows and what it leaves to a real repository; a signature whose key is not on the machine is recorded as not checked; a replacement is asked in place of a dead repository; the open review findings are each placed in this brief or the cleanup list; the skill's logic is a tested command; changes to the runner itself are shown in throwaway repositories. The acceptance test is a representative sample (six S cases from their pins and empty caches, and the eight measured cases again), with the whole batch left to a later run. One independent review at the end, with cheaper checks before the acceptance test.

On outside requests the user's rule is a preference, not a prohibition: 'If we can avoid downloading outside stuff, we should, for efficiency and consistency.' The gates name mirrors on this machine alone, which need no permission since the commit before this one, and report what was asked outside. The user declined a machine switch that turns outside fetching off ('a rabbit hole that could have other side effects'); VF-083 records the question, what holds today, and what there is to weigh when it comes up again. The brief builds no such switch.

The results page of the jobs line points at the new brief, lists the day's later decisions, and says the redirect rule has its first test. The operating notes' link to the brief is repointed. Verified: every link and anchor of the new brief resolves; the tests the change selects, 10 of 10 Python test files; retired.py check reports nothing. The claim in VF-083 that S48's gate asks Maven Central was read from the committed gate record (2 files, 9.6 MB).
